result.text: Title: Ordering in an Online Shop A customer that logs into an E-Shop system and has to wait for its login confirmation (its credentials are checked by the system).
If the login was successful then the customer can continue to select products, else the shopping experience stops.
After selecting a product the customer has to add it to a shopping cart, save the product and check if every product was already selected.
These steps repeat until all products were selected.
Then the order is finished by the shopping system and simultaneously payment and shipment for the order is prepared.
For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

result.rule: When the description states that, within one branch of a parallel split, a participant must wait until an external party confirms something (for example, a bank confirming a payment) before the branch can continue to the parallel join that precedes the next step: Model the wait as an intermediate catch event on that branch, placed after the activity that starts the wait and before the branch's sequence flow into the parallel join. Do not drop the wait or leave that branch without a sequence flow into the join. Do not replace the wait with an exclusive gateway or move it outside the parallel split.

When the description says an action requests something from an outside party or source, and a later step can only proceed once that party's arrival or delivery happens at an unspecified or uncertain time: Model the request as its own task. Model the arrival or delivery as a distinct intermediate catch event placed after the request task and before the step that depends on it. Do not merge the request and the arrival into one element, do not represent the wait as a task or as internal work of another activity, and do not omit the request task. If the request is made on a parallel branch, keep the catch event on the path that leads to the dependent step.

When the description states that the process must receive or confirm an incoming item, result or notification from outside before it continues, and that receipt or confirmation is itself a step with its own consequences for the next activities: Model that step as a receive task (bpmn:receiveTask) placed in the flow at the point where the description states it, rather than as a bare intermediate catch event, and keep the following activities connected to it. Use a catch event only when the description describes a pure timing or condition wait with no work attached to the receipt.

When the description describes a step where the process waits, phrased as an activity (for example 'awaiting' an outcome) and names no message, signal, timer or condition that is received: Model this waiting step as a task in the sequence, placed after the preceding activity and before the next step, with sequence flows connecting it on both sides. Do not replace it with an intermediate catch event, and do not add a flow from the preceding activity directly to the next gateway that skips the task. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description names a specific message, signal, timer or condition to be received.

result.rule: Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.

result.rule: When The description says that a step can only continue once other people have responded, for example when it says to continue only after responses have been received, or until a required number of people have replied.: Model an intermediate catch event that waits for those responses, placed after the activity that requests them and before the decision or activity that depends on them. Do not replace the wait with a task or a gateway. Keep the activity that acts on the responses as a separate element after the catch event.

When the description describes a step where the process waits, phrased as an activity (for example 'awaiting' an outcome) and names no message, signal, timer or condition that is received: Model this waiting step as a task in the sequence, placed after the preceding activity and before the next step, with sequence flows connecting it on both sides. Do not replace it with an intermediate catch event, and do not add a flow from the preceding activity directly to the next gateway that skips the task. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description names a specific message, signal, timer or condition to be received.

When the description says a participant is held at a step until a specific, explicitly named condition becomes true (for example, that it is their turn), and the description states that condition as the thing being awaited: Model the pause as an intermediate catch event labeled with the named condition as the description words it. Place it after the step that precedes the pause and before the participant's next step, with sequence flows on both sides. Do not model the pause as a task.

When the description says an action requests something from an outside party or source, and a later step can only proceed once that party's arrival or delivery happens at an unspecified or uncertain time: Model the request as its own task. Model the arrival or delivery as a distinct intermediate catch event placed after the request task and before the step that depends on it. Do not merge the request and the arrival into one element, do not represent the wait as a task or as internal work of another activity, and do not omit the request task. If the request is made on a parallel branch, keep the catch event on the path that leads to the dependent step.
